CHINA PRESS.
DEC 1 6 1938
00535
Date
Local Cotton
Mills Said In
Boom Period

Purchasing Power Of
Laborers' Wages
Decreased

By JOHN AHLERS

Local cotton mills, during the last five months of the past year, had to suffer much from the war, but this year Shanghai's cotton industry appears to be doing remarkably well. There are indications that the profits of local cotton spinning of late months have been nothing less than extraordinary.

This applies to western-owned, Japanese, and Chinese plants as well. Ewo Mills, just effecting a new issue of shares, are at the present foremost in the public eye and deserve our attention first.

For its current business year, Ewo Mills paid an interim dividend of 75 cents per share. A final dividend of surely not less, and perhaps even more, is in sight; the company reports net profits of working for the first nine months of this calendar year to the amount of $4,500,000.

* Stock Dividend Paid

These dividends will amount to almost ten per cent of the present quotation of Ewo Mills shares in the local stock market. In addition, however, there is a sort of stock dividend being paid to Ewo's shareholders in connection with the issue of the new Ewo shares.

The new Ewo shares are being offered to shareholders at $14 while the market value of Ewo shares is $3 higher. The old shareholders will cash that difference, which to them will amount to another dividend of almost 20 per cent.

Thus Ewo Mills will pay out to shareholders this year nearly 30 per cent of the market price of Ewo shares in the form of various dividends, and a still much higher percentage of the nominal value of Ewo shares. Obviously, this is an extremely prosperous year for the company.

Japanese Earn Well

But local Japanese cotton mills earn at least as well. Pre-war extent of their employment has been restored, and the five mills of Shanghai Cotton Manufacturing Co. alone have about 16,000 employees working day and night.

pending. Ewo Mills are executing a vast program of modernization of machinery and buildings in existing plants, and some new ventures are being started upon. The Japanese mills expand. Of the Chinese mills, the Sung Sing Cotton Mill No. 9 is constructing a three-storied new building. The Tata-controlled Tung Yih Cotton Mill is proposing to construct a new weaving shed.

There can be no doubt that most of the local cotton mills are having a very good time just now. What is the source of their apparent extraordinary prosperity?

Prices of cotton yarn and cotton piece-goods have increased very considerably as a consequence of the local devaluation of the Chinese currency. So has the price of raw cotton. But wages have not increased to the same extent and, in some instances, appear to have even been lowered.

Wages Said Low

Reliable information is available on the wages being paid in the Chinese-owned mills. Wages paid in the British and Japanese mills are said to be slightly higher, but they were higher also prior to the war. Nominal wages and purchasing power of those wages appear to have suffered the same fate in all the cotton mills whatever nationalities the proprietors are.

In the following table, the first column of figures represents average hourly wage rates paid in local currency in Shanghai Chinese-owned cotton mills last year.

The second column is giving the wages being paid at present, also in local currency. The third column is showing the "real wages" paid today as calculated in pre-war purchasing power, considering the fact that the purchasing power of $1 paid in wages to the average Shanghai worker, through the large increase in the cost of living, has decreased since the outbreak of the war by about 30 per cent.

《字林西报》。
1938年12月16日
00535
日期
本地棉
纺厂据称处于
繁荣时期

劳工工资的
购买力
下降

作者：JOHN AHLERS

去年最后五个月，本地棉纺厂深受战争之苦，但今年上海的棉纺织业似乎表现极佳。有迹象表明，近几个月来本地棉纺业的利润可谓非凡。

这同样适用于外资、日资和华资工厂。怡和纱厂刚刚发行新股，目前最受公众关注，值得我们首先注意。

在本营业年度，怡和纱厂支付了每股75仙的中期股息。最终股息肯定不少于该数额，甚至可能更多；公司报告显示，本历年前九个月的营业净利润为4,500,000美元。

* 支付股票股息

这些股息总额几乎相当于怡和纱厂股票在当地股市当前报价的百分之十。此外，随着怡和新股的发行，还有一种形式的股票股息支付给怡和的股东。

新股以14美元的价格向股东配售，而怡和股票的市场价值高出3美元。老股东将兑现这一差额，对他们而言，这相当于另外近20%的股息。

因此，怡和纱厂今年将以各种股息的形式向股东支付相当于怡和股票市场价格近30%的收益，以及相当于怡和股票面值更高比例的收益。显然，这对该公司来说是极其繁荣的一年。

日资企业获利丰厚

但本地日资棉纺厂的盈利至少同样丰厚。其战前的雇佣规模已恢复，仅上海纺织株式会社旗下的五家工厂就有约16,000名员工日夜工作。

待定。怡和纱厂正在现有工厂实施大规模的机器和建筑现代化计划，并启动了一些新项目。日资工厂也在扩张。在华资工厂中，申新第九棉纺织厂正在建造一栋三层新楼。由塔塔集团控制的统益纱厂提议建造一个新的织布车间。

毫无疑问，大多数本地棉纺厂目前的境况非常好。它们表面上的非凡繁荣源于何处？

由于中国货币在当地贬值，棉纱和棉布的价格大幅上涨。原棉价格也是如此。但工资并未同比例上涨，在某些情况下，甚至似乎有所下降。

据称工资偏低

关于华资工厂支付的工资，有可靠的信息来源。据说英资和日资工厂支付的工资略高，但在战前也较高。无论业主国籍如何，所有棉纺厂的名义工资及其购买力似乎都遭遇了同样的命运。

在下表中，第一列数字表示去年上海华资棉纺厂以当地货币支付的平均小时工资率。

第二列给出的是目前支付的工资，同样以当地货币计算。第三列显示的是按战前购买力计算的今日“实际工资”，考虑到这样一个事实：由于生活成本大幅增加，自战争爆发以来，支付给上海普通工人的1美元工资的购买力下降了约30%。

CHINA PRESS.
OCT 26 1938
Settlement Employs
140,000 Workers In
Month Of September
Nearly 140,000 hands were employed in the various industrial concerns situated in the International Settlement and on extra-Settlement Roads during the month of September, it was revealed yesterday. The exact figure is placed at 139,846.
While not as high as the figures last year, the total shows an increase of 1,556 as compared with statistics for August.

（批：File 26/10）

虽然不及去年的数字，但总数较八月份的统计数据增加了1,556人。

11 8 38

Settlement Employment
Figures Reveal Steady
Increase For Last Month

While employment figures in the
Settlement proper showed a steady
increase last month, there was a
slight increase in unemployment in
Chinese and outside areas for the
same period, it was revealed by the
Industrial Department of the
Shanghai Municipal Council yester-
day.
Workers in the Settlement dur-
ing June numbered 130,000, it was
stated, while last month they had
risen to 137,000. Including these
the total figure for the Settlement
and outside areas, Pootung, Nantic
and Chapei, so far as could be
ascertained, was 142,000 for June
and 148,000 for July.
According to these figures, while
the Settlement employment figures
rose by 7,000, the figures for the
whole area rose by only 6,000, thus
indicating a drop of 1,000 in em-
ployment in the Japanese occupied
zones.
Employed in the Settlement in
July last year were between 220,000
and 250,000 workers, while in the
whole area, between 325,000 and
350,000 were employed.

19/8
Tilo
8/8
page_data.zh:
00265
8039A/C
1938年8月11日

租界就业
数据显示上月稳步
增长

上海公共租界工部局工业科昨日透露，虽然上月租界核心区的就业数据显示稳步增长，但同期华界及外围地区的失业人数略有增加。
据悉，6月份租界内的工人数量为130,000人，而上月已增至137,000人。包括这些数字在内，据查明的租界及外围地区（浦东、南市和闸北）的总人数，6月份为142,000人，7月份为148,000人。
根据这些数据，虽然租界的就业人数增加了7,000人，但整个区域的就业人数仅增加了6,000人，这表明日军占领区的就业人数减少了1,000人。
去年7月，租界内的受雇工人介于220,000至250,000人之间，而整个区域的受雇工人介于325,000至350,000人之间。

8月19日
蒂洛
8月8日

REPORT Date: May 13, 1938
Subject Working conditions in Wayside District due to Sino-Japanese
hostilities.
Made by L.I. Bennett. Forwarded by [Signature] C/S

Sir,

Prior to August 1937, the commencement of Sino Japanese
hostilities there were 131 industrial concerns of varying
natures in operation in Wayside District, employing a total
of more than 20,000 Chinese employees.

Of these industrial concerns 112 were of Chinese ownership,
the larger proportion of Chinese employees being employed in
these concerns.

The above total of Chinese employees does not include
the permanent and daily casual labour at the many wharves in
Wayside District, or in the various godowns which are indirectly
connected with the shipping industry, which amount to thousands
of employees.

Again in addition to coolies etc; employed in the shipping
and transportation industries which are connected with the
godowns, there were many small factories, usually in converted
dwelling houses, consisting of engineering workshops, black-
smiths, motor repair and painting shops and the textile indus-
tries etc; which found employment, both for unskilled and
skilled labour, this inclusive of the apprentices etc;
employed in various shops in Wayside District would amount to
approximately a total 40,000 employees employed in Wayside
District all of whom were thrown out of work in August 1937
at the commencement of hostilities.

During the period of hostilities between 40% to 50%
of Wayside District north of Broadway wherein the majority
of these industrial concerns and shops etc; were located was
completely destroyed by fire, a total of 35 listed factories
being practically completely destroyed by fire, a further 4

报告 日期：1938年5月13日
主题：因中日敌对行动导致的路边区工作状况。
制作人：L.I. Bennett（音译）。转发人：[签名] C/S

先生：

在1937年8月中日敌对行动开始之前，路边区有131家各种性质的工业企业正在运营，共雇佣了20,000多名中国雇员。

在这些工业企业中，有112家为华人所有，大部分中国雇员受雇于这些企业。

上述中国雇员总数不包括路边区众多码头以及各种与航运业间接相关的仓库中的固定工人和每日临时工，这类人员数量达数千人。

此外，除了受雇于与仓库相关的航运和运输行业的苦力等人员外，还有许多小型工厂，通常由住宅改建而成，包括工程车间、铁匠铺、汽车修理和喷漆店以及纺织工业等；这些工厂为非技术工人和技术工人提供了就业机会，若包括在路边区各店铺受雇的学徒等人员，路边区受雇人员总数约为40,000人，这些人均在1937年8月敌对行动开始时失业。

Hung Fun Cotton Weaving Factory (恒丰) 832

Previous to hostilities in 1937, other than shipping
interests there were few industrial concerns of Japanese
ownership in Wayside District.
There are at present about approximately 3,500 employees
of various concerns working in Wayside District, the majority
of whom live in Shanghai, South of the Garden Bridge, either
proceeding to their employment via river, motor transportation
provided by their respective employers or on foot, very few
residing in the District, which is due to early curfew for
Chinese residents, lack of accommodation, transportation and
marketing facilities, as in the large proportion of residential
areas of this type of workers which have been destroyed and in
cases where premises are not destroyed, lack of water and
lighting upon the premises.
Whilst these existing conditions last, with the additional
presence of Japanese troops and marines the re-habilitation of
Wayside District will be a long time before returning to any-
thing approaching normal conditions.

在1937年战事之前，除航运利益集团外，杨树浦地区很少有日资工业企业。
目前约有3,500名各公司雇员在杨树浦地区工作，其中大多数人居住在上海外白渡桥以南，要么通过水路前往工作地点，要么乘坐各自雇主提供的机动车，或者步行，极少有人居住在该区，这是由于对中国居民实行早期宵禁、缺乏住宿、交通和市场设施，因为此类工人的大部分居住区已被摧毁，而在房屋未被摧毁的情况下，又缺乏水电供应。
只要这些现状持续存在，加上日军和海军陆战队的驻扎，杨树浦地区的复兴将需要很长时间才能恢复到接近正常的状况。

代表申新纱厂的荣尔仁（Yung Er Zung）先生和顾鼎吉（Koo Ding Jih）先生表示，他们未曾与日本人或代表日本人行事的华人进行过任何沟通。但他们确实声明，位于华德路1316号的第五纱厂已于1938年3月出租给美商联合证券公司（Associated Securities），地址为汉密尔顿大厦208号。5月4日上午致电奥尔曼·戴维斯与科普斯事务所（Allman Davies and Kops）的奥尔曼（Allman）先生时，他证实了从申新产业手中接管第五纱厂一事。他进一步表示，如果该厂开工，将在美方管理之下，且他们目前正在为运营做准备。
位于平凉路2545号的詹森制革厂（Jansen Leather Tannery）在过去两个月里一直在日方管理下运营，目前雇佣了一百四十二名华籍员工。新建了建筑物，几乎每天都能观察到皮革运输活动。

顾火昌（Koo Huo Tsang）的住所，5月4日特别巡佐史蒂文斯（Stevens）和华籍侦探第108号曾前往该处，一名职员告知他们，制革厂是在业主知情的情况下运营的，他认为业主当时正在平凉路的工厂内。通过电话与顾火昌联系时，他以忙碌为由推迟了面谈。
位于首尔路110号的成华棉纺厂目前正由五十名男性和二百三十名女性华籍员工运营。经理俞楚松（Yu Chu Sung）在接受问询时表示，他已与日本当局做出安排，从而可以运营该厂。
据信俞楚松以某种方式与维新政府有关联，因此受到日本当局的特殊照顾。值得一提的是，在最近几个月里，不像永安和申新纱厂那样，该工厂未有日本人进入。
位于杨树浦路1578号的久记建筑承包商是一家华资企业，但自战事爆发以来，雇佣了一名日籍人士松本（Matsumoto）先生，他目前经营着一个小型木材锯切部门，用于军事目的，雇佣了十名华籍员工。此举是在业主知情的情况下进行的。

Factories
Plan
Reopening

Preparations are now being made
by several concerns owning fac-
tories in Yangtzepoo and Pootung
to start operations, and it is hoped
that the whistles can start blowing
very soon.
According to a late survey of the
Industrial Section of the S. M. C.,
recently published, the undamaged
factories in the Yangtzepoo area
are capable of absorbing about 40,-
000 workers when full operations
are resumed.
Together with the 56,000 workers
of Shanghai who now have work,
this number would aggregate up-
wards of 100,000, about one-third of
the number of workers employed
before the beginning of hostilities
here. The employment of this
additional number would help in
some measure the vast unemploy-
ment problem with which the city
is now faced.
The re-employment possibilities
lie mostly with factories manufac-
turing for export, there being little
trade at present to absorb goods
manufactured for domestic use.
A number of the larger factories
have re-opened and have taken
on skeleton forces to make
necessary repairs and put machin-
ery in good order preparatory to
resuming full operations. A few of
the factories have also taken on a
few operatives to start the wheels
rolling.
page_data.zh:
工厂
计划
复工

几家在杨树浦和浦东拥有工厂的公司
目前正在筹备开工，希望很快就能
响起开工汽笛声。
根据工部局工业组最近发布的一项
最新调查，杨树浦地区未受损的工厂
在全面恢复运营时，可吸纳约40,000
名工人。
加上目前已有工作的56,000名上海
工人，这一总数将超过100,000人，
约占战事开始前在此就业工人总数
的三分之一。新增这些就业机会将在
一定程度上缓解本市目前面临的巨
大失业问题。
再就业的可能性主要存在于面向出
口制造的工厂，因为目前几乎没有
贸易来消化内销商品。
一些较大的工厂已经重新开业，并
雇佣了骨干人员进行必要的维修，
整理机器设备，为全面恢复运营做
准备。少数工厂还雇佣了一些操作
工，开始启动运转。

During the months of September and October, 1937, seven
offices for the registration of unemployed workers were
established at the following addresses by the Shanghai
Municipality Unemployed Workers' Relief Committee, which was
formed under the auspices of the Chinese Authorities :-
(1) Lane 1216, 9 Avenue Edward VII.
(2) Shanghai Western District Social Centre, 4200 Robison Road.
(3) No.1429 Brenan Road, O.O.L.
(4) Office of the Peasants' and Labourers' Life Improvement
Association, 52 Kong Foh Li, Brenan Road, O.O.L.
(5) No.5 Heng An Fang, Fang Pang Road, Nantao.
(6) Kwan Tieh Miao, a temple situated at 174 Zao Chia
Road, Nantao.
(7) Kung Woo Theatre, Fang Pang Jao, Min Kuo Road, Nantao.

As a result of the evacuation of the Chinese troops
from Shanghai, all these registration offices have been
closed down.

It is reported that the Shanghai Municipality
Unemployed Workers' Relief Committee has rented Post Box
No.902 for communication purposes, although the Postal
Authorities are reluctant to confirm this information. So far
no person has yet been seen obtaining mail from the box, and
it is believed that arrangements have been made between the
postal authorities and the Shanghai Municipality Unemployed
Workers' Relief Committee for the delivery of letters.

C. D. I.

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers: 27-10-37(am)

RELIEF OF UNEMPLOYED

Acting on instructions received from the
Shanghai City Government, the Bureau of Social Affairs
recently ordered the Unemployed Workers' Relief Committee
to draw up certain plans for the relief of unemployed
workers.

The Bureau has now received a reply from
the Unemployed Workers' Relief Committee, giving the
plans of relief. These plans have been submitted to
the City Government for consideration.

It is learned that 10,000 male adult-
workers will be registered and a number of camps will
be established for their accommodation. Registered
unemployed workers who are eligible for certain duties
will be given an allowance of 10 cents each.

REPORT
Date Nov,14, 37.
Subject Re Strike at the Cheng Kong( ),Silk Weaving Factory,
situated at 577/131 Connaught Road.
Made by D.S.I.Chu Meng Wei, & Forwarded by Inspector,i/c.

Sir,
At 6.15 p.m Nov.14,1937,Mr. Loh Ih Van( ),
Manager of Cheng Kong Silk Weaving Factory at 577/131 Connaught
Road,made a report at the station to the effect that the
workers of the above mill had gone on strike at 4 p.m. even date.
A party of Police attended,the following being ascer-
tained:-
At the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese hostilities,
the management of the factory intended to cease functioning,but
the workers requested the manager Loh Ih Van to allow them to
continue work to the understanding that their wages be cut from
$1.60 to 90 cents per roll of silk. The manager granted the
request and an agreement was drawn up and signed by all the
workers.
Owing to the present shortage of the weaving materials
the management continued operations by borrowing from other
factories. The workers anticipating that the factory would be
forced to close in the near future due to lack of raw materials,
presented Mr. Loh Ih Van, the manager,with the following demands:
(1) Each worker be paid $1.60 per roll.
(2) Each worker be advanced $35.00.
The manager refused to entertain these demands result-
ing in the workers,113 in number (96 male & 17 females) going
on strike at 4 p.m. even date and refusing to leave the pre-
mises. On arrival of police,however,they dispersed peacefully.
Uniform P s have been posted at the entrance to the
factory as a precautionary measure. No untoward incident
occurred. Special Branch informed.

D.D.O."B" Division.
Copy sent to Sp.Br.
D.S.I.

由副巡官朱孟伟（Chu Meng Wei）呈报，经督察长转呈。

先生：
1937年11月14日下午6时15分，位于康纳脱路577/131号的成公丝织厂经理罗义万（Loh Ih Van，音译）先生到捕房报案，称该厂工人于当日下午4时罢工。
一队警察到场，查明情况如下：
中日战事爆发之初，厂方本打算停止运营，但工人请求经理罗义万允许他们继续工作，条件是他们的工资从每卷丝绸1.60元降至90分。经理同意了这一请求，并起草了一份协议，由所有工人签署。
由于目前编织材料短缺，管理层通过向其他工厂借用材料来维持运营。工人预料工厂将因缺乏原材料而在不久的将来被迫关闭，遂向经理罗义万提出以下要求：
(1) 每卷工资支付给每位工人1.60元。
(2) 每位工人预支35.00元。
经理拒绝考虑这些要求，导致113名工人（96名男性及17名女性）于当日下午4时罢工，并拒绝离开工厂 premises。然而，警察到达后，他们和平散去。
作为预防措施，制服警察已在工厂入口处站岗。未发生任何意外事件。已通知特别科。

“B”区副总监。
副本送特别科。

day shift, but now in order to increase our produce we intend
to commence night work. During the night the factory, up to
the 7th floor, will be lighted and as Japanese troops are now
in occupation of the Chapei area, we wish to know if there will
be any danger or whether the Japanese troops have any objection
to our starting night work.

Please inform us and thank you.

Foh Sing No.7 Flour Mill.

D.S. S.B.
D.S.

Yue Chin Tse representative of the Foh Sing
No 7 Flour mill seen by D.S. S.B.
and informed no objection.
D.S.R. 10/11

Sin Wan Pao and other local Newspapers :- 25-10-37(PM)

SILK FILATURES TO RESUME OPERATIONS

As it is difficult to dispose of their present
stocks of cocoon, the owners of silk filatures located
inside the Settlement to the north of the Soochow Creek
are planning to resume operations and to work from 5 a.m.
to 5 p.m. daily.
It is learned that the Feng Foong (凤丰) Silk
Filature will resume operations as from October 26. The
Heh Yue (合裕) Silk Filature will resume as soon as repair-
to its machinery have been completed.
page_data.zh:
《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：1937年10月25日（下午）

缫丝厂将恢复运营

由于难以处理现有的蚕茧库存，位于苏州河以北租界内的缫丝厂业主正计划恢复运营，每日工作时间为上午5时至下午5时。
据悉，凤丰缫丝厂将于10月26日起恢复运营。合裕缫丝厂将在其机器维修完成后尽快恢复运营。

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers: 22.9.37 (P.M.)
COTTON MILLS IN WESTERN DISTRICT MAY RESUME NIGHT OPERATIONS
In view of the fact that more production should
be effected at this time when a major war of resistance
on all fronts has broken out, the Wing On, the Yu Hsin
and the Sun Sin Nos.1, 2 and 9 Cotton Mills in the Western
District resumed day operations at the beginning of
September. It is now learned that with a view to maintain-
ing the livelihood of their workers and in order to effect
an increase in production in the interests of the nation,
these cotton mills are planning to resume night operations
in the near future.
page_data.zh:
《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：1937年9月22日（下午）
西区棉纺厂可能恢复夜间作业

鉴于目前全面抗战爆发，应加强生产，西区的永安、裕信及申新第一、第二和第九棉纺织厂已于9月初恢复日间作业。现获悉，为了维持工人生计并为了国家利益增加产量，这些棉纺厂计划在近期恢复夜间作业。

page_data.en:
Ta Kung Pao (Evening Edition) :- p.m. 11-9-37
300,000 UNEMPLOYED WORKERS IN SHANGHAI

A large number of workers have been thrown out
of employment following the outbreak of the hostilities in
Shanghai.
According to a careful estimate, there were
between 17,000 and 18,000 workers employed by the various
factories in the International Settlement prior to the war
and the majority of these factories are located in the
Eastern and Northern Districts. As these two districts
have been converted into war zones, about 15,000 labourers
are rendered jobless following the closure of their factories.
Taking into account the unemployed labourers
of those factories situated in areas adjacent to the
International Settlement, the total number of unemployed
workers now in Shanghai will be not less than 300,000.
page_data.zh:
《大公报》（晚刊）:- 1937年9月11日下午
上海有30万失业工人

随着上海战事的爆发，大量工人失业。
据仔细估算，战前公共租界各工厂雇佣的工人介于17,000至18,000人之间，且大多数工厂位于东部和北部地区。由于这两个地区已变为战区，约15,000名劳工因工厂关闭而失业。
考虑到公共租界邻近地区工厂的失业劳工，目前上海的失业工人总数将不少于30万人。

As it is located at a place which is regarded

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 1, Special Branch
REPORT
Date August 17, 1937
Subject Unrest among the employees of the Commercial Press.
Made to C.D.I. Sih Tee-liang Forwarded by

The employees of the Commercial Press Sales Office
and Factory, which have suspended business following the
outbreak of hostilities in Shanghai, have been agitating
for a relief allowance. At 10 a.m. August 16, some 100
workers congregated in the Head Office, Honan Road, to press
their demand for the issue of this allowance, but were
eventually persuaded to leave the place at about 12.20 p.m.
August 16, after the Management had promised to consider
their request.
The Management have decided to issue an allowance at
the following rate:-
1. Those workers whose services are to be retained while
the hostilities last, will be issued their wages, but
with a deduction varying from 30% to 60%.
2. Those workers whose services will be temporarily
dispensed with, will be issued an allowance ranging
from 40% to 50% of their wages.
3. That the wages and allowances will be issued in two
instalments, on the 15th and at the end of every month.
Wages for the month of August will be issued at the
godown of the Commercial Press, 306 Canton Road (Central
District) on August 17, commencing from 10 a.m.
Mr. Chao Ping-nien(曹冰巖), representative of the
Management, who communicated the foregoing information visited
Police Headquarters, and requested that protection be afforded
them while the wages were being paid out.

D.C. (Special Branch)
C. D. I.

报告
日期 1937年8月17日
主题 商务印书馆雇员中的不安情绪。
呈报给特别股主任督察施德良（Sih Tee-liang） 经转呈

商务印书馆发行所和印刷厂自上海战事爆发后停业，其雇员一直要求发放救济津贴。8月16日上午10时，约100名工人聚集在河南路总管理处，坚持要求发放此津贴，但在资方承诺考虑其请求后，最终于8月16日下午12时20分左右被劝离。
资方决定按以下标准发放津贴：-
1. 那些在战事持续期间保留职务的工人，将发放工资，但扣除30%至60%不等的金额。
2. 那些暂时解雇的工人，将发放相当于其工资40%至50%的津贴。
3. 工资和津贴将分两次发放，即每月15日和月底。
八月份的工资将于8月17日上午10时开始，在商务印书馆位于广东路306号（中区）的仓库发放。
资方代表曹冰巖（Chao Ping-nien）先生通报了上述信息，并访问了警察总局，要求在发放工资期间为他们提供保护。

Special Branch,
August 15, 1937.

LOCAL FACTORIES AND SHOPS - UNEMPLOYMENT SITUATION

At the beginning of August, a number of factories
located in the Settlement, especially in the Eastern District,
suspended operations as a result of the tenseness of the local
situation. On August 13, following the outbreak of hostilities
in Chapei between Chinese and Japanese forces, practically all
industrial concerns suspended operations. It is estimated that
approximately 130,000 workers employed by various factories in
the Settlement and 60,000 employees of industrial concerns in
Chinese controlled territory are now unemployed. The approxi-
mate number of unemployed workers distributed in the Settlement
is as follows :-

| Cotton Mill Workers | Silk Filature & Silk Weaving Workers | Engineering & Iron Factory Workers | Others |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 90,000 | 6,000 | 10,000 | 24,000 |

It is reported that approximately 40% of the workers
employed in Settlement factories returned to their native places
prior to the outbreak of the hostilities.

Approximately 50,000 shop assistants in the Settlement
are now unemployed.

CERTIFIED TRUE COPY.

...G.J. Richards...

GHY/

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Yangtszepoo Station,
REPORT
Date August 13, 1937.
Subject Unusual gathering of night duty workers outside Yu Foong
Cotton Mill 2866 Y'poo Road.
Made by D.S. Duke Forwarded by [Signature] Inspt. O. i/c

Sir,
At 12.55 p.m. 13/8/37 a telephone message was received
from the Yu Foong Cotton Mill, 2866 Y'poo Road, reporting
that their night shift workers had collected outside the
mill and were demanding their pay.
A party of Police under Inspector Andrew and D.S.I.
Crighton at once proceeded to the scene where it was
learned that the workers had heard rumours that the Kung
Dah Mill had closed and was paying its workers to-day.
This evidently made the Yu Foong night duty workers a little
apprehensive as to their own position and so they returned
to their mill and asked for their wages, although these
would not normally be paid them until next Tuesday.
It was explained to the workers that there was no
intention of closing down the mill to-day, that it was
impossible to obtain their wages from the bank at such
short notice, and that they would probably receive full
payment to-morrow. This contented the workers and they
had dispersed to their homes by 1.30 p.m. without any
untoward event having occurred.
The Yu Foong management subsequently telephoned the
station with the information that they had managed to
secure the necessary cash from the bank and would commence
paying wages to-morrow morning (14/8/37).
I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
[Signature]

事由：杨树浦路2866号裕丰纱厂外夜班工人异常聚集。
呈报人：警佐杜克（Duke） 转呈人：[签名] 督察 O. i/c

先生：
1937年8月13日下午12时55分，接杨树浦路2866号裕丰纱厂电话报告，称该厂夜班工人聚集在厂外，要求发放工资。
由安德鲁（Andrew）督察和副警司克里顿（Crighton）率领的一队警察立即赶赴现场，经了解得知，工人们听到谣传，称公大纱厂已停工并于当日向工人发放工资。这显然使裕丰纱厂的夜班工人对自己的处境感到有些担忧，因此他们回到厂里要求发放工资，尽管按惯例工资通常要等到下周二才发放。
向工人们解释说，今日并无关闭工厂的打算，且因时间仓促，无法从银行取出现金支付工资，但他们很可能在明日获得全额支付。工人们对此表示满意，并于下午1时30分散回家，期间未发生任何意外事件。
随后，裕丰纱厂管理层致电巡捕房，告知他们已从银行设法取得必要现金，并将于明日上午（1937年8月14日）开始发放工资。
此致，
敬礼

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Yangtszepoo Station,
REPORT
Date Aug. 14th, 19 37.
Subject Labour trouble at China Aluminium Rolling Mills.
Made by D.S.I. Crighton Forwarded by [Signature] officer i/c.
Sir,
I beg to report that at 1.30 p.m. 13-8-37, a telephone
message was received from above factory, a foreign concern,
located at 610 Meichow Road, to the effect that all employees
had struck work and were demanding their wages. Further that as
result of the trouble created by them the Russian Police Watchman
employed therein had been forced to fire one shot from his
pistol.
On receipt of this information a party of police under
Sub-Insp. Mancarrow, proceeded to the scene and managed to
question the workmen numbering approximately 300 strong.
As result of enquiries made by the undersigned, it was
ascertained that after the workmen had partaken of their
mid-day meal, they refused to start work and demanded all wages
owing to them. The manager fearing serious trouble requested
them to leave the factory and to wait outside while he
arranged for the paying of wages. This was agreed to and all
left the factory, however on arrival outside one or two of the
ringleaders in the movement commenced damaging the managers car
which was sitting outside. Seeing this Russian Watchman No.20,
Vassilieff, rushed outside and in an attempt to prevent serious
damage to the car used a certain amount of force, which was
retaliated to, by several of the Chinese workmen who tore his
tunic etc. managing to free himself he ran back into the factory,
but before he could close the gates, the workmen, who by this
time had been worked up in to a fighting spirit, stormed the
gate, with result that he pulled his pistol and fired one shot
into the air. This had the necessary effect of dispersing the
crowd and permitting the watchman to close the gates.
（批：S.I. / DBR / 14/8）
（右上角手写：Their File No. 192）

杨树浦巡捕房，
报告
日期：1937年8月14日。
事由：中国铝轧厂劳资纠纷。
呈报人：副警司克里顿（Crighton） 转呈人：[签名] 负责警官。
先生：
谨报告，1937年8月13日下午1时30分，接上述位于梅周路61号的外商工厂电话，称所有员工罢工并要求发放工资。此外，由于他们制造的骚乱，受雇于该厂的俄国巡捕被迫用手枪开了一枪。
接到此信息后，由曼卡罗（Mancarrow）副督察率领的一队警察赶赴现场，并对大约300名工人进行了询问。
经卑职调查查明，工人在用完午餐后，拒绝开工并要求支付所有欠薪。经理担心发生严重骚乱，要求他们离开工厂并在外面等候，以便他安排发放工资事宜。工人们同意了这一要求并全部离开工厂，然而一到外面，此次行动的一两名头目便开始损坏停在外面的经理汽车。见此情景，20号俄国巡捕瓦西里耶夫（Vassilieff）冲了出去，试图阻止对汽车造成严重破坏，使用了一定的武力，但遭到几名中国工人的反击，他们撕破了他的制服等物。他设法脱身后跑回工厂，但在他关上大门之前，此时已被激怒、充满斗狠情绪的工人冲击大门，结果他拔出手枪向空中开了一枪。此举起到了驱散人群的必要效果，并使巡捕得以关上大门。
（批注：S.I. / DBR / 14/8）
（右上角手写：他们的档案号 192）

Enquiries were made amongst the workers, but none were
found to be suffering from bullet wounds and all were more
or less corroborated the watchmans statement that he had fired
the shot into the air.
The said watchman who appeared to be badly shaken, was
brought to station, where he made the attached statement.
The workers, who on arrival of police were questioned down
were then told that they would receive their wages at 4 p.m.
and as a result left the vicinity.
Later enquiries revealed that all wages had been paid and
that all workers had left the premises quietly, after which
the factory was closed down.
In conclusion I wish to add that the watchman stated he
would call at Headquarters on the morning of 14-8-37 when he
would render his resignation.
The pistol in question a .38 auto. 'Colt' No.10455
S.M.P. No.1401 has been detained at Yangtszepoo Station.
I am, Sir,
Yours obediently
John. Crighton

在工人中进行了调查，但未发现有人遭受枪伤，且所有人或多或少都证实了巡捕关于他是向空中开枪的陈述。
该巡捕似乎受到严重惊吓，被带至巡捕房，并作出了附后的陈述。
警察到达时对工人进行了讯问，随后告知他们将在下午4时领取工资，工人们因此离开了该地区。
后续调查显示，所有工资均已支付，所有工人均在平静中离开厂区，之后工厂关闭。
最后，我想补充一点，该巡捕表示他将于1937年8月14日上午前往总部递交辞呈。
涉案手枪为一支 .38 口径自动“柯尔特”手枪，编号10455，警务处编号1401，已扣押在杨树浦巡捕房。

Date Aug. 13, 1937.
Subject. Incidents Resulting from Sino-Japanese Hostilities.
Made by D.S.I. McCaney. Forwarded by

Sir,
At 5.30 p.m. August 13, 1937 two male Chinese
(1) Tseu Mau Kai (周茂楷), 32, Shanghai, m/Rice-
shop assistant, 221 East Kashing Road O.O.L.
(2) Yang Joong (楊木公) 42, Nanking, S/Hawker,
243 Thorburn Road.
surrendered to police station handcuffed together.
Questioned, the 1st described stated that he had been
arrested by officers of Lingping Road Sub-station S.C.G.P.
Bureau at 5 p.m. Aug. 12th at his home on suspicion of being
concerned in supplying rice to Japanese. The 2nd described
stated that he had been arrested by the same authorities at
about 1 a.m. Aug. 13th in Chapel on suspicion of having
defrauded a number of Coolies of money on pretext of introducing
them to work in the Chapel Water and Power Works.
Both men stated that at about 5 p.m. even date the whole
Lingping Road Station staff evacuated throwing the cell gate
open and telling them to go free.
No charge had been preferred against them nor did the
evacuating authorities wait to remove their handcuffs.
Handcuffs were removed and retained at Wayside Station.
1st described was identified by staff of the Zung
Tah (森泰) Rice Shop, 67 Muirhead Road.
Address of 2nd described visited and verified by Wei
Wan Fah (魏渭法) master of Sung Tah (森泰) Coal Shop on
ground floor.
D.O. "D" Div. Mr. Maker was informed of particulars of case.
Owing circumstances and information received by Special
Branch to effect, prisoners, in custody of S.C.G.P.B. for

日期：1937年8月13日。
事由：中日敌对行动引发的事件。
呈报人：副督察长 McCaney。转呈人

先生，
1937年8月13日下午5时30分，两名中国男子
(1) 周茂楷 (Tseu Mau Kai)，32岁，上海人，职业：米店助手，住址：东嘉兴路221号 O.O.L.
(2) 杨木公 (Yang Joong)，42岁，南京人，职业：小贩，住址：韬朋路243号。
双手铐在一起向巡捕房自首。
经讯问，第一人称述者称，他因涉嫌参与向日本人供应大米，于8月12日下午5时在其家中被华界公安局临平路分所警员逮捕。第二人称述者称，他因涉嫌以介绍去 Chapel 水电厂工作为借口诈骗多名苦力钱财，于8月13日凌晨1时许在 Chapel 被同一当局逮捕。
两人均称，当日下午5时许，临平路巡捕房全体职员撤离，打开牢门并告知他们自由离去。
当局未对他们提出任何指控，撤离时也未等待解开他们的手铐。
手铐已在汇山巡捕房解开并保留。
第一人称述者已由缪尔黑德路67号森泰 (Zung Tah) 米店职员辨认确认。
第二人称述者的住址已由一楼森泰 (Sung Tah) 煤号老板魏渭法 (Wei Wan Fah) 走访核实。
"D" 区警务官 Maker 先生已获知本案详情。
鉴于特别课收到的情报显示，华界公安局拘留的因轻微罪行入狱的囚犯正在某些地区被释放，这两名男子于晚上8时被允许离开。

At 6 p.m. 13th D.S. Taylor reported that the Japanese
Naval Landing Party stationed on the Ration Stores, 229 Baikal
Road (corner of Paoting Road) were preventing traffic from
proceeding along those roads.
At 7 p.m. S.I. Radinoff and D.S. Smith visited vicinity

extinguish Road lights with bamboo poles and stones.
They were prevented from proceeding along Baikal Road by
motorcycle although S.I. Radinoff was in uniform.
Majority of factories in district have suspended work
owing to situation and failure of workers to show up for work.
Very few shops etc are doing business openly. Many of them
have packed their stock and left the district.

large numbers of Japanese refugees aboard left Shanghai on Aug.

The river steamer S.S. "Ping Wo" with Chinese refugees

Sir,
The district remained normal during the 24 hours ending
6 a.m. 11-8-37.
Very few refugees were observed to be evacuating from adjoining
Chinese Territory.
Several families are reported to have removed during the day
from lanes in the vicinity of East Yuheng Road.
The following business establishments have closed:-
Ching Wo Industrial Material Supply Store, 652 Dixwell Road.
Yoon, Chong Hardware Shop, 186 Suchow Road.
Yue Chong Second Hand Store, 167 Dixwell Road.
Dong Ho Exchange Shop, 110 Urge Road.
Moh Chong Machinery Shop, 10-12 Urge Road.
Three refugees from Chinese Territory are reported to be
residing at the An Loh Lodging House, Suchow Road.
The recent incident does not appear to have alarmed
the residents in this District to any great extent.
Several pawnshops are reported to have ceased business again.
Rhui

Landing of Japanese troops.
At about 3 p.m. Aug. 10th two war vessels of cruiser type
tied up at the O.S.K. wharf.
A number of troops, stores and munitions were disembarked.
Some three or four hundred of the troops and stores proceeded
east on Yangtzepoo Road by motor truck.
During the evening until after 9 p.m. a further number of
troops disembarked from war vessels tied up in the river at
Wayside Public Jetty, Ewo Road. It is estimated that about 1,000
officers and men landed with full kit and stores.
A total of 2,824 Chinese refugees passed South through
and/or from Wayside district per various types of vehicles
between 7 a.m. 11 and 7 a.m. Aug. 12th.
D.S.I.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE. Misc. File No. 321.
Wayside Station,
REPORT
Date. Aug. 8, 1937.
Subject. Suspension of Work by Factories and Movements of Refugees.
Made by. D.S.I. McCahey. Forwarded by. E. J. Lees Supt.

Sir,
The Sing Hwo (顺和) Towel Factory, 232 Tongshan Road suspended business on August 7th owing to present strained situation. A total of 27 employees, 5 male and 22 female, are effected. They all intend returning to Kading. Manager of the factory is Tseu Ching Foo (崔祥甫).
The 60 employees, 35 male and 25 female, of the Yuen Tsung (永成) Silk Factory, 253 Dent Road have requested the manager Ching Ching Sung (陈金顺) close down and advance them three months wages to enable them to return to their native province Szechuen. Negotiations are in progress.
A total of 240 Chinese, mostly students, arrived per C.P.R. s.s. Empress of Asia at 1.15 p.m. August 7th from Japan, 230 from Yokohama and 10 from Kobe. On disembarkation at the Shanghai and Hongkew Wharf several were questioned by D.S. Smith and detectives with reference to their return. All stated that they had left Japan of their own free will.
During twenty four hours 7 a.m. 7th to 7 a.m. 8th August 6,487 Chinese refugees passed through and/or from Wayside district via Broadway E.-Yuenfong, E.Seward-Yuenfong and Tongshan-Singkeipang Roads.
Various types of vehicles were being used to transport their belongings.

Senior Det 1/o G.J.S.H. John Cahey D.S.I.
D.D.O. "D"

汇山巡捕房，
报告
日期：1937年8月8日。
主题：工厂停工及难民流动情况。
呈报人：副督察麦卡希（McCahey）。转呈人：警司E. J. Lees。

敬启者：
位于同山路232号的顺和（Sing Hwo）毛巾厂因当前紧张局势于8月7日停止营业。受影响雇员共27人，其中男性5人，女性22人。他们均打算返回嘉定。该厂经理为崔祥甫（Tseu Ching Foo）。
位于丹徒路253号的永成（Yuen Tsung）丝厂的60名雇员（男性35人，女性25人）要求经理陈金顺（Ching Ching Sung）关闭工厂，并预支三个月工资，以便他们返回原籍四川省。目前正在进行谈判。
8月7日下午1时15分，共有240名中国人（大多为学生）乘坐加拿大太平洋铁路公司（C.P.R.）的“亚洲皇后号”轮船从日本抵达上海，其中230人来自横滨，10人来自神户。在上海码头和虹口码头卸船时，史密斯副督察（D.S. Smith）及侦探就其回国事宜对其中数人进行了询问。所有人均表示是自愿离开日本的。
在8月7日上午7时至8月8日上午7时的二十四小时内，共有6,487名中国难民经由百老汇路-元芳路、东熙华德路-元芳路以及同山路-新吉邦路，穿过或离开汇山地区。
各类车辆被用于运输他们的财物。

高级侦探 G.J.S.H. John Cahey 副督察

to our starting night work.

be effected at this time when a major war of resistance 
on all fronts has broken out, the Wing On, the Yu Hsin 
and the Sun Sin Nos.l, 2 and 9 Cotton Mills in the Western 
District resumed day operations at the beginning of 
September. It is now learned that with a view to maintain- 
ing the livelihood of tneir workers and in order to effect 
an increase in production in the interests of the nation, 
these cotton mills are planning to resume night operationge 
in the near future.

Internatio:.al Settlement, the total number of unemployed 
workers now in Shinghai will be not less than 300,000.
